grade_reason: The only AI-related material found since January 2025 is two co-signed letters, one on military use of AI in targeting and one on data center electricity costs. Nothing found acknowledges catastrophic risk from AI, and nothing dismisses it.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. No statement by Whitehouse on superintelligence, extinction, loss of control, bioweapons, AI safety, a pause or a China agreement was found; absence in search results is not proof that none exists, and hearing remarks (he sits on the Judiciary Committee) and floor speeches were not searched transcript by transcript. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: no source found shows him as a co-sponsor; search results named no Senate co-sponsors at all, and Congress.gov was not checked, so this is 'not shown' rather than confirmed absent. Both quotes are from letters he co-signed, not his personal words. The two press release pages were opened through a page-fetch tool that returns text via a summarising model; I asked it twice for the exact sentences and the wording matched, but a reviewer should confirm the quotes character for character on the pages. The Iran letter sentence appears in the release's introduction ending in a comma and in the letter text ending in a full stop; the letter version is used. The fetch tool listed 46 signer names for the Iran letter while the release says 44; not resolved. A December 2024 letter on fast-tracking AI data centers is outside the date range and was left out. Older hearing transcripts from 2023-2024 that list him as a committee member were not used.
